text.p: British Biotech Plc said on Wednesday that late-stage clinical trials showed its lead product Lexipafant had a "significant" impact on acute pancreatitis, which causes failure of the liver and kidneys.

In a telephone interview with Reuters after announcing "positive" European test results for its lead product, Finance director James Noble said Lexipafant's impact on organ failure was "significant," adding "that is as good as you can hope for."
Analysts were reserving judgement on the announcement until they were given a more detailed breakdown of the trial results at a meeting with the company this morning.
However, news that British Biotech was on schedule to have its first product on sale in 1998 boosted its volatile share price, which rose 5 1/2 pence to 230 pence in mid-morning trade.

Lexipafant accounts for well under 10 percent of most analysts' valuations of the company, which are dominated by the novel anti-cancer drug Marimastat which is now in late-stage trials. But Noble said the news on Lexipafant "is incredibly important. It changes us from a company that has a pipeline of ideas to one that should have a product on the market by 1998."
Noble said he was "comfortable" with analysts' forecasts for peak sales of Lexipafant of around $300 million a year.
